subject: Priming thresholds + canary ramp readout for private deployment
messages:
From: Marcus Hargreaves <m.hargreaves@acmecloud.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: ACME Platform Team <platform+acme@acmecloud.com>
Date: 2028-11-16T08:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Priming thresholds + canary plan — quick sync

Marissa / Karthik,

Thanks for walking through the private deploy plan this morning. We've run a few internal sims and noticed two items that could affect priming:

- KV cache seeding: our traffic pattern has a long-tail on prefix reuse. Without a warm prefix set we see initial 2–3s tail latency on spot checks.
- MTU mismatches between our edge (MTU 9000) and your VPC transit (MTU 1500) — we saw fragmentation during stress that can drop packet reassembly for large batched requests.

We're happy to run a gated canary but wanted to confirm your thresholds: what hit-rate do you want for KV cache before we increase traffic from 2% -> 10% -> 50%? Also, any ops playbook to remediate MTU mismatches quickly?

Attaching our short result CSV from the sim.

Regards,
Marcus
Platform Lead, AcmeCloud
(Attachment: canary-sim-results.csv [csv])

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Hargreaves <m.hargreaves@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-11-16T09:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Priming thresholds + canary plan — quick sync

Marcus — thanks for the sims and callout. Short answers up front:

- Target KV cache warm hit-rate: >= 92% on our generation prefix histogram for the first 10 minutes at each ramp step. If we fall below 88% we pause the ramp and run a re-seed job.
- MTU: our ops runbook includes an MTU verification step and fallback to 1500 on the transit interface if fragmentation is detected. We'll share a one-page checklist.

Action items I propose:
1) We run a 2% canary for 20 minutes and collect the token-latency distribution + KV hit-rate.
2) If hit-rate >= 92% and P95 latency < 350ms we proceed to 10% for 30 minutes.
3) If the 10% step passes, ramp to 50% with continuous traffic shadowing and rollback alarms enabled.

I've attached our priming playbook (v2) with the exact metric queries and remediation steps. Karthik / Vivek — please confirm the MTU remediation snippet and whether we should add an eBPF drop counter probe to the baseline.

Thanks,
Marissa
Senior PM, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
(Attachment: priming-playbook-v2.pdf [pdf])

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Hargreaves <m.hargreaves@acmecloud.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-11-16T10:18:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Priming thresholds + canary plan — quick sync

Folks — quick technote:

- MTU approach: agree with fallback to 1500. We'll implement an active probe that sends a 9k UDP packet to the edge and watches for ICMP fragmentation-needed. If frag is observed, we automatically announce a transit MTU override for the session and mark the run as "manual remediation" in the canary ticket.
- eBPF probe: we'll add a simple drop counter on the ingress veth and export to prometheus as redwood.network.mtu_frag_drops. Threshold: >5 drops/min during ramp will trigger the rollback.

Also adding a KV-seeding detail: run a prioritized prefix seeder that loads the top 10k prefixes from the client's sample set (we'll leverage your sim csv). Seeder runs in parallel to the 2% canary and should finish within 7 minutes on our standard pool. If it doesn't, we hold the ramp.

I'll paste the small ops snippet here for Marcus to vet:

-----BEGIN FORWARDED MESSAGE-----
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: platform+acme@acmecloud.com
Date: 2028-11-16T10:18:00-08:00
Subject: MTU probe and remediation snippet

1) Run UDP MTU probe: send 9000B packet to edge IP, wait 5s for ICMP frag-needed.
2) If frag-needed, run transit-interface: ip link set mtu 1500 && notify ops.
3) Trigger one-off KV re-seed with prefix list from sim.

-----END FORWARDED MESSAGE-----

Karthik
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Hargreaves <m.hargreaves@acmecloud.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-11-16T12:00:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Priming thresholds + canary plan — quick sync

Confirming infra readiness:

- We pre-seeded a small pool last night on staging and validated that seeding time scales linearly with number of prefixes. 10k prefixes consistently finishes in 6–8 minutes.
- Observability: created dashboards for token-latency, KV-hit-rate, eBPF mtu drop counter, and NIC retransmit rate. Alerts: p95 latency > 600ms OR KV-hit-rate < 85% will automatically cut traffic and flip to warm standby.
- Bridge ops snippet attached (small shell commands and expected outputs).

I recommend we run the 2% canary at 14:00 PT today and meet at 14:40 for a short readout. If Marcus is comfortable with the MTU probe being non-blocking, we can proceed.

-Vivek
Head of Cloud Infra
(Attachment: bridge-ops-snippet.txt [text])

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Hargreaves <m.hargreaves@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-11-16T14:41:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Priming thresholds + canary plan — quick sync — readout scheduled

Marcus — thanks, all set for the 14:00 PT 2% canary. Quick checklist we will follow during the 40-minute window:

- Start: kick off prioritized prefix seeder (verify completion in 10m).
- Monitor: KV hit-rate (goal >= 92%), token p95, mtu_frag_drops.
- Ops watch: if mtu_frag_drops > 5/min or p95 > 350ms -> immediate pause and rollback.
- Decision: at 14:40 we decide to progress to 10% or abort.

I'll post the live dashboard link in the meeting invite and record the canary run in the linked Drive folder. If the canary is green we'll follow the ramp plan in the playbook.

See you on the bridge.
Marissa
Senior PM, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
(Drive link: https://drive.redwood.ai/s/ACME-Canary-Run-2028-11-16)
